hero.headline: DHS considers blocking international flights at San Francisco, Newark airports
hero.body:
The Department of Homeland Security is developing plans to restrict international arrivals at San Francisco International Airport and potentially Newark Liberty International Airport, according to multiple reports. The proposal represents an effort to pressure jurisdictions that limit local cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.

The potential restrictions have prompted warnings from airlines and business groups about widespread travel disruption. Industry representatives cautioned that blocking international flights at major airports could create chaos for travelers and commerce.

The measures appear aimed at sanctuary jurisdictions, cities and counties that have policies limiting how local law enforcement assists federal immigration authorities. San Francisco and Newark are both located in areas with such policies.

The proposal faces significant opposition and logistical challenges. Critics have raised concerns about the economic impact on affected regions and the practical difficulties of redirecting international air traffic. Airlines warned that rerouting flights would strain capacity at other airports and disrupt travel schedules.

Questions have also emerged about how the restrictions would affect the World Cup, though specific details about that interaction remain unclear based on discussions reported in media coverage.

The Department of Homeland Security confirmed it is drawing up plans for the restrictions but has not announced a final decision or timeline for implementation. The agency oversees Customs and Border Protection, which processes international arrivals at U.S. airports.

San Francisco International Airport serves as a major gateway for trans-Pacific travel and handles millions of international passengers annually. Newark Liberty is one of three major airports serving the New York metropolitan area and plays a similar role for transatlantic flights.

The restrictions would represent an unprecedented use of federal authority over air travel to enforce immigration policy. Previous administrations have not attempted to block international arrivals at specific airports as a pressure tactic against local governments.

Business groups expressed alarm at the potential economic consequences. International flight restrictions could affect tourism, business travel, and cargo operations at the targeted airports, with ripple effects throughout their regional economies.

cards.headline: Trump Expected to Announce Decision on Iran Nuclear Deal Soon
cards.teaser: President Trump said he would make a final determination soon on whether to move forward with an agreement with Iran to end the war.
cards.body:
President Trump met with his advisers after US and Iranian officials confirmed they had agreed on a framework for a deal. However, no announcement followed the meeting. Trump has indicated he will make a final determination soon, though he has wavered on whether to proceed with the agreement.

The potential deal aims to end the conflict between the US and Iran. Trump's indecision has left the Middle East uncertain about the agreement's future and whether it will move forward.

cards.headline: Hegseth Tells Asian Allies US Commitment Depends on Increased Defense Spending
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told Asian military leaders at a Singapore security conference that greater defense contributions would determine access to US assistance.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth addressed concerns about US commitment to Asia at a security summit in Singapore, reassuring allies that America is "not turning back" on the region. He told military leaders that those willing to increase defense spending and capabilities would receive priority access to US assistance and arms deals.

Hegseth also expressed alarm about China's military buildup while stating the US does not seek "needless confrontation." His remarks directly addressed regional leaders' questions about American priorities and their access to future military support.

cards.headline: US, UK, Australia to develop underwater drone technology under Aukus pact
cards.teaser: The three nations will develop drones aimed at protecting undersea cables and strengthening naval defense capabilities.
cards.body:
The United States, United Kingdom, and Australia are collaborating on underwater drone technology as part of their Aukus military partnership. The initiative aims to protect undersea cables and strengthen naval defence capabilities among the three nations.

This project expands the scope of Aukus cooperation, addressing vulnerabilities in critical underwater infrastructure that the allies view as strategically important.

cards.headline: SpaceX Wins $4.16 Billion Space Force Contract for Satellite Network
cards.teaser: The U.S. Space Force awarded SpaceX a contract to build satellites that will track airborne targets from orbit.
cards.body:
SpaceX received a $4.16 billion contract from the U.S. Space Force to build and deploy satellite sensors capable of detecting and tracking airborne targets from space. The missile-tracking satellites will enhance military commanders' ability to identify threats across wide areas and are part of the Space Based Airborne Target Indicator program.

The satellites are designed to integrate with the Pentagon's planned "Golden Dome" defense system. SpaceX serves as the prime contractor for the project, handling both satellite construction and launch operations.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary disputes claim Iran war delayed Taiwan arms sale
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth rejected assertions from a military official that ongoing conflict with Iran has delayed a $14 billion arms sale to Taiwan. Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao told senators the United States was postponing the deal to protect shrinking munitions supplies.

Hegseth's public disagreement with his acting Navy secretary's testimony highlights internal tensions within the Pentagon over military readiness and weapons inventory management. The split between the two senior defense officials has drawn attention to how the Iran conflict is affecting America's ability to support its allies.

Taiwan has been awaiting the arms package as part of long-standing American commitments to help defend the island against potential military threats. The sale represents one of the largest pending weapons transfers to the region.

Cao's testimony to senators suggested that sustained combat operations in Iran have strained U.S. weapons stockpiles significantly. He indicated the Pentagon needed to carefully manage munitions inventories and restrict major foreign arms sales to address supply concerns.

Hegseth's pushback against this characterization raises questions about whether Pentagon leadership agrees on the severity of weapons supply challenges. The public nature of their disagreement is unusual for the department's top officials.

The timing of the Taiwan sale has become more significant as the United States maintains military operations against Iran. American forces engaged in the conflict consume precision munitions and other weapons systems at substantial rates. Earlier this month, President Trump said he expected additional U.S. military deaths before the Iran conflict concludes, describing casualties as inevitable in war.

The conflict has extended beyond military concerns into economic territory. Energy bills are rising for millions of households, with typical users facing an additional 221 pounds annually under new price caps. U.S. inflation increased at its fastest pace in three years in April, driven largely by higher energy prices tied to the war. Disposable household income has dropped for three consecutive months after adjusting for inflation.

The economic impact is affecting public opinion on Trump's leadership. A Reuters/Ipsos survey showed the president's approval rating fell to near its lowest level since returning to office, with declining support even among Republicans. Trump won the 2024 election largely on promises to reduce inflation.

Neither Hegseth nor Cao has provided specific details about current stockpile levels or the particular weapons systems included in the Taiwan package. The disagreement became public when Hegseth responded to Cao's Senate testimony.

The dispute underscores broader challenges facing the Pentagon as it balances immediate military needs in the Middle East with longer-term commitments to support allies in Asia. Taiwan's defense capabilities remain central to broader U.S. strategic interests in the region.

cards.headline: Credit card delinquencies reach highest level since 2011
cards.teaser: More than 13 percent of credit card balances were at least 90 days past due in the first quarter.
cards.body:
The share of credit card balances at least 90 days past due climbed above 13 percent in the first quarter. That represents the highest delinquency rate since 2011.

The increase in seriously delinquent accounts signals growing financial stress among cardholders. The last time late payment rates reached this level was during the aftermath of the financial crisis.

hero.headline: Ebola Outbreak Surges in Remote Mining Town as Medical Workers Struggle to Contain Spread
hero.body:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ituri province has spiraled into a public health crisis, with nearly 1,000 suspected cases and more than 220 suspected deaths reported. The head of the World Health Organization has called for an immediate ceasefire among armed groups to help contain the disease.

Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the WHO director general, traveled to the DRC this week, describing the situation as a "catastrophic collision of disease and conflict." The outbreak was confirmed on May 15 in Ituri, the nation's most northeastern province, which borders South Sudan and Uganda. As of the latest updates, 101 cases had been confirmed with authorities investigating more than 3,000 possible contacts.

The death rate is substantial. WHO officials estimate the mortality rate at between 30 percent and 50 percent among confirmed cases. Aid group Save the Children highlighted that a quarter of confirmed deaths were children, calling for urgent scaling up of infection prevention measures.

The mining economy of the region has contributed to the outbreak's spread. Ituri attracts migrant workers to its gold mines, making the population transient and harder to track. This movement has facilitated transmission to neighboring provinces, with cases now appearing in rebel-held areas of North Kivu and South Kivu.

Armed conflict in the region has severely complicated containment efforts. Medical teams face attacks on health facilities and widespread community distrust. Health workers have reported critical shortages of essential supplies including personal protective equipment, body bags, soap, and chlorine. A doctor in Butembo reported having only two body bags remaining and said staff had purchased additional supplies with their own money.

Cultural practices have also hindered the response. Traditional burial rituals involve families washing and touching bodies, but Ebola victims remain highly contagious after death. When authorities have restricted bodies for safe disposal, community members have attacked health facilities. In Mongbwalu, unidentified individuals burned patient isolation tents on Saturday, causing 18 Ebola patients to flee. Seven more patients escaped on Sunday, with one suspected case dying during the escape.

Uganda has responded to the threat by closing its border with the DRC for four weeks, except for Ebola response teams and humanitarian operations. The country had reported seven confirmed cases as of Sunday, with one death. Uganda authorities require anyone authorized to enter from the DRC to undergo mandatory self-isolation for 21 days.

The WHO has urged all warring parties to agree to a ceasefire, emphasizing that stopping Ebola transmission depends entirely on humanitarian access. Without it, ongoing clashes will continue driving mass displacement and severing critical containment corridors.

cards.headline: Four More Men Rescued From Flooded Cave in Laos After Week-Long Ordeal
cards.teaser: Rescuers freed four additional men from a flooded cave in Laos where they had been trapped for more than a week, with two still missing.
cards.body:
Four more miners have been rescued from a flooded cave in Laos, bringing the total freed to five of the seven men trapped underground. The miners entered the narrow cave tunnels on May 20 while searching for gold before becoming trapped by rising water. The rescue operation has required divers to navigate through muddy water, sharp rocks, and dangerously narrow passages to reach the trapped individuals.

Two villagers remain missing as rescue teams continue their efforts deeper into the cave system. The operation has involved draining water from the cave and managing collapse hazards to safely extract the trapped miners.

cards.headline: Trump Expected to Announce Decision on Iran Nuclear Deal Soon
cards.teaser: President Trump said he would make a final determination soon on whether to move forward with an agreement with Iran to end the war.

President Trump met with his advisers after US and Iranian officials confirmed they had agreed on a framework for a deal. However, no announcement followed the meeting. Trump has indicated he will make a final determination soon, though he has wavered on whether to proceed with the agreement.

cards.headline: Japan Tightens Immigration Rules, Forcing Some Foreign Business Owners to Leave
cards.teaser: New visa rules under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi are requiring some foreign business owners who have established themselves in Japan to depart the country.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has implemented new visa rules that are affecting foreign business owners in Japan. The immigration crackdown has caught curry shop owners among those impacted by the policy changes.

Some foreign entrepreneurs who have put down roots in Japan and established businesses are now being forced to leave under the new regulations. The tightened immigration policies represent a shift in how Japan handles foreign residents who operate businesses in the country.

cards.headline: Vietnamese Leader Calls for Better China Ties to Support Regional Security
cards.teaser: Vietnam's top leader said improved relations with China could help advance peace and security in the region.
cards.body:
Vietnam's top leader stated that better ties with China can contribute to regional peace and security. The comments came as Asian leaders gathered to discuss security concerns and the risks of superpower conflict in the Asia Pacific.

The Vietnamese president emphasized that the Asia Pacific region seeks responsible commitment from major powers. His remarks addressed broader concerns about how relationships between major powers affect stability in the region.

cards.headline: Ye and Travis Scott Concerts Canceled in Italy Over Security Concerns
cards.teaser: Italian authorities canceled concerts by Ye and Travis Scott, citing the need to ensure public order and safety.
cards.body:
Italian authorities canceled scheduled concerts by Ye, formerly known as Kanye West, and Travis Scott. The events were called off to ensure public order and safety, according to officials.

Jewish leaders had objected to the concert by Ye, who has a history of antisemitic remarks. The security concerns led authorities to make the decision to cancel both performances.

cards.headline: White House releases Trump physical exam results
cards.teaser: President Trump's physician said he is in excellent health following a checkup, though recommended weight loss and more exercise.
cards.body:
President Trump remains in excellent health according to a memo from his physician, Dr. Sean Barbabella, released by the White House. The examination found strong cardiac, pulmonary, neurological and overall physical function.

The memo noted Trump is experiencing lower leg swelling and benign hand bruising. Despite these minor issues, the president's doctor confirmed he is fit to serve in office.

cards.headline: New DNA test could help millions avoid chemotherapy for breast cancer
cards.teaser: An international trial found a new screening test could identify breast cancer patients who can safely skip chemotherapy.
cards.body:
Revised Card Text

A new genomic test could allow millions of breast cancer patients to avoid chemotherapy, according to an international trial. The screening tool can identify patients with low test scores who can safely receive hormone therapy alone, achieving nearly identical health outcomes to those who undergo chemotherapy.

The findings could transform treatment guidelines worldwide. Currently, chemotherapy is typically recommended after surgery when doctors assess there is a risk of disease recurrence. This test offers a way to spare many patients from the side effects of chemotherapy while maintaining their treatment effectiveness.

cards.headline: Liverpool fires coach Arne Slot one year after Premier League title
cards.teaser: The club dismissed Slot after two seasons, with Andoni Iraola emerging as the leading candidate to replace him.
cards.body:
Liverpool have sacked head coach Arne Slot after two seasons in charge, just a year on from winning the Premier League title. The dismissal marks an unexpected end to Slot's tenure despite the recent success he achieved with the club.

Andoni Iraola is the leading candidate to become Liverpool's next manager.

cards.teaser: The three nations will develop drones aimed at protecting undersea cables and strengthening naval defense capabilities.

The United States, United Kingdom, and Australia are collaborating on underwater drone technology as part of their Aukus military partnership. The initiative aims to protect undersea cables and strengthen naval defence capabilities among the three nations.

cards.headline: 15-year-old girl dies after swimming at beach
cards.teaser: Chiedza Nyanjowa died following a beach swimming incident, her family said.
cards.body:
A 15-year-old girl died after swimming at a beach. Chiedza Nyanjowa's family described her as a bubbly person with a kind spirit.

The family released a statement remembering Nyanjowa following her death. Authorities have not released additional details about the circumstances of the incident.

cards.headline: Pride celebrations face funding pressures as corporate sponsorships decline
cards.teaser: Companies are pulling back from public LGBTQ+ support as it becomes politically risky, a public relations expert said.
cards.body:
Pride celebrations across the country are experiencing financial strain as corporate sponsorships decline. According to public relations experts, companies are increasingly viewing public support for the LGBTQ+ community as politically risky, leading them to withdraw funding from Pride events.

This shift in corporate behavior represents a significant change from previous years, when business sponsorships were a traditional and reliable funding source for Pride organizations. The reduction in corporate backing has created substantial challenges for event organizers attempting to maintain their celebrations.

hero.headline: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes on Launch Pad, Threatening NASA Moon Mission Timeline
hero.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a static fire test at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday evening, destroying the launch pad and potentially disrupting NASA's plans to return astronauts to the Moon within the next two years.

The explosion occurred at 9pm ET during the scheduled "hotfire" test at Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 36. A massive fireball engulfed the pad seconds after the test began, creating an orange sky visible from Fort Pierce, 115 miles away. Shockwaves from the blast were felt across Florida's space coast, with residents in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach reporting that their homes shook. The explosion was even visible to observers hundreds of miles north in South Carolina.

Blue Origin described the incident as "an anomaly" and confirmed that all employees were safe and accounted for. Company founder Jeff Bezos acknowledged the setback on social media, stating "It's too early to know the root cause but we're already working to find it" and pledging to "rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying."

The New Glenn rocket is central to Blue Origin's role in NASA's lunar program. The company won a contract to launch lunar landers for NASA missions, and is competing with SpaceX to provide the lander for the Artemis IV mission scheduled for 2028, which would represent the first crewed Moon landing since the Apollo program ended in 1972. Artemis III, planned for 2027, will test Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander against SpaceX's Starship Human Landing System to determine which vehicle will transport astronauts from the Orion capsule to the lunar surface.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman stated that the agency would conduct a full evaluation of program timelines following the explosion. "Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult," he posted, adding that NASA would work with partners to support an investigation and assess near-term mission impacts.

This explosion marks the latest challenge for Blue Origin as it competes with SpaceX for NASA contracts. The company faced previous setbacks, including a payload placement error during a recent flight that resulted in temporary grounding by the Federal Aviation Administration. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared the rocket to resume operations.

Flames continued burning at the launch pad more than two hours after the explosion. Emergency officials reported no immediate hazards to surrounding areas from fumes or other potential dangers. Blue Origin has constructed large new facilities near Cape Canaveral to support crewed and cargo missions in partnership with NASA, but the company now faces an investigation into the explosion's cause before resuming launch operations.

cards.headline: Dell Stock Hits All-Time High as AI Demand Drives Revenue
cards.teaser: Dell Technologies shares reached a record after the company reported strong quarterly results driven by artificial intelligence products.
cards.body:
Dell Technologies stock surged to an all-time high after the company delivered results that exceeded expectations for its first quarter of fiscal 2027. The rally added $34 billion to founder Michael Dell's personal wealth, making him richer than Mark Zuckerberg according to wealth trackers.

The company attributed its performance to increased demand for AI-related hardware and infrastructure. Dell has positioned itself as a supplier of servers and computing equipment needed to run artificial intelligence applications. The results set up what analysts described as an important week for AI-focused technology stocks.

cards.headline: United Airlines Flight Diverted After Passenger Allegedly Attempts Cockpit Breach
cards.teaser: A United Airlines flight made an unscheduled landing in Madison, Wisconsin, after a passenger was detained for trying to access the cockpit.
cards.body:
United Airlines flight 2005 from Chicago to Minneapolis diverted to Madison after crew members detained a passenger who allegedly attempted to breach the cockpit. Authorities arrested the passenger after the plane landed. Audio recordings from the flight indicated the incident involved a cockpit breach attempt.

The airline classified the individual as an unruly passenger. Law enforcement met the aircraft upon arrival in Madison and took the person into custody. United has not released additional information about the passenger's actions or potential charges.

cards.headline: China Expands Digital Yuan Use to Lottery and Government Spending
cards.teaser: China is broadening applications for its central bank digital currency beyond retail transactions.
cards.body:
China has extended the use of its digital yuan to include lottery draws and fiscal spending by government entities. The expansion represents an effort to increase adoption of the central bank digital currency beyond consumer payments. Officials are testing the digital yuan in new use cases as part of a gradual rollout.

The moves come as China continues developing its digital currency infrastructure while other countries watch the experiment. The digital yuan allows the Chinese government to track transactions and provides an alternative to traditional banking systems. China has been piloting the currency in select cities and applications since 2020.

cards.headline: Biotech Firm Replimune to Resubmit Cancer Drug After FDA Talks
cards.teaser: Replimune plans to ask regulators for a third review of its melanoma drug following what the company called productive discussions with the FDA.
cards.body:
Replimune will resubmit its cancer drug for FDA approval after the agency twice rejected the application. The company said it held productive talks with FDA officials following a shakeup at the regulatory agency. The stock jumped 80 percent on news of the resubmission plan.

The FDA had previously rejected the melanoma treatment, but Replimune believes changes in agency leadership and review procedures may lead to a different outcome. The company did not specify what modifications it will make to the application. The FDA has not publicly commented on the discussions or indicated whether its position on the drug has changed.

cards.headline: China's Biotech Industry Growth Alarms U.S. Drug Developers
cards.teaser: Clinical trials conducted in China are drawing attention at a major oncology conference as the country's pharmaceutical sector expands.
cards.body:
Research from Chinese biotech companies received attention at an international oncology gathering in Chicago, highlighting the country's growing presence in drug development. Clinical trials originating in China are increasing in number and sophistication, according to presentations at the meeting.

The expansion of China's biotechnology sector has raised concerns among U.S. researchers and companies about declining American dominance in pharmaceutical innovation. China has invested heavily in life sciences research and development, building laboratory

hero.headline: Trump administration proposes coal ash monitoring changes
hero.body:
The Trump administration wants to shift coal ash monitoring and enforcement responsibilities to state governments and allow states to bypass national standards. Environmental groups turned out in force to oppose the proposed rollbacks.

Coal ash is the waste material left behind after burning coal at power plants. The substance has been regulated at the federal level to prevent contamination of groundwater and other environmental hazards.

The proposed changes would reduce federal oversight by relying on individual states to monitor and enforce coal ash disposal rules. States would also gain the ability to set their own standards instead of adhering to uniform national requirements.

Environmental advocates organized significant opposition to the proposal. The turnout reflects concerns about potential weakening of protections that currently exist under federal regulations.

Coal ash contains heavy metals and other toxic substances that can leach into water supplies if not properly contained. Federal standards were established to create consistent safeguards across the country, particularly for communities near coal-fired power plants and disposal sites.

The shift to state-level control raises questions about enforcement capacity and consistency. Different states would be able to implement different levels of protection, potentially creating a patchwork of standards across the nation.

The proposal comes as the Trump administration has pursued various rollbacks of environmental regulations. Coal ash management has been a point of contention between industry groups seeking flexibility and environmental organizations pushing for stronger protections.

Public comment periods typically allow citizens and organizations to weigh in on proposed regulatory changes before they are finalized. The strong turnout from environmental groups indicates this proposal will face organized resistance during the review process.

cards.headline: Volcanic eruption may provide method to address planet-heating gas
cards.teaser: A violent volcanic eruption may have revealed a new approach to tackle a potent greenhouse gas.
cards.body:
Scientists believe a violent volcanic eruption has provided insights into a potential new method for addressing a potent planet-heating gas. The discovery emerged from studying the eruption and its effects.

The finding could represent a new tool in efforts to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions. Volcanic activity created conditions that researchers believe may be replicable for climate purposes.

cards.headline: Book examines history of vaccine opposition movements
cards.teaser: A new book explores the long history of people who have opposed vaccines across different eras.
cards.body:
A newly published book traces the historical roots of vaccine opposition, examining the figures and movements that have resisted immunization campaigns over time. The work categorizes opponents into different groups based on their motivations and beliefs.

The book identifies three main types of vaccine opponents: grifters who exploit fears for profit, cynics who distrust medical authority, and true believers who hold genuine convictions against vaccination. This framework helps explain the persistence of anti-vaccine sentiment across generations.

cards.headline: Indian court ruling revives criticism of Google ad business
cards.teaser: Founders have seized on an Indian court ruling to renew criticism of how Google operates its advertising business.
cards.body:
An Indian court ruling has energized company founders and critics who argue it validates long-standing concerns about Google's advertising practices. The decision focused on how platforms handle trademarked keywords in their ad systems.

Legal experts said the ruling could prompt platforms to reconsider their policies around trademarked keywords. Critics contend that current practices allow competitors to bid on trademarked terms, potentially confusing consumers.

cards.headline: Windows 11 introduces customizable Start menu in test build
cards.teaser: Microsoft has released a new Windows 11 build featuring a fully customizable Start menu design.
cards.body:
Windows 11 users testing experimental builds can now access a new Start menu that allows full customization. The update introduces a modular, resizable design that lets users adjust the layout to their preferences.

The changes are available on the Experimental Channel for testers. Microsoft announced the new builds as part of an initiative to revamp Windows 11, which also includes a movable Taskbar feature.

cards.headline: TikTok expands features in push toward super app status
cards.teaser: TikTok may be working to become an all-purpose app that people use for most of their digital activities.
cards.body:
TikTok is working to become a super app—a platform where users can handle most of their digital activities in one place. The company is expanding beyond its core short-form video service to offer additional functionality.

Super apps combine multiple services such as messaging, payments, and shopping alongside content. This model has found success in Asian markets, and TikTok is adapting the approach for its global audience.

cards.headline: Enhanced Games allows performance-enhancing drugs in competition
cards.teaser: A sporting competition where most athletes used performance-enhancing drugs took place, drawing interest from the tech industry.
cards.body:
The Enhanced Games held a competition in which a majority of athletes openly used performance-enhancing drugs. The event represents a departure from traditional sports, which ban such substances.

The competition has attracted attention from Silicon Valley, particularly around peptides and other enhancement technologies. Organizers believe the model could establish a new business approach that the tech industry is ready to embrace.

hero.headline: Liverpool fires head coach Arne Slot after two seasons
hero.body:
Liverpool parted ways with head coach Arne Slot with immediate effect after two seasons in charge. The club won the Premier League title during his tenure but decided to dismiss him. Andoni Iraola emerged as the leading contender to replace Slot.

Slot's departure marks a swift reversal of fortune. Chief football writer Phil McNulty described it as one of the most remarkable falls from grace in Premier League history. The club has already approached Iraola about taking over the position.

Liverpool did not provide specific reasons for the dismissal in their statement. The decision came despite Slot delivering a league title during his time at Anfield. The firing happened just two years after he was appointed to lead the club.

The timing of the dismissal surprised many observers given the recent success. Slot took charge of Liverpool and managed to secure the Premier League championship. His inability to maintain the authority wielded by his predecessor Jürgen Klopp reportedly factored into the decision.

Iraola currently works as a manager and has been identified as the front runner for the vacant position. Liverpool moved quickly to make contact with him following Slot's departure. The club aims to finalize a replacement in the coming days.

The dismissal caps a turbulent period for Slot, who experienced both triumph and termination in a short span. His two-season tenure included the highest achievement in English club football but ended abruptly. Liverpool now enters a search for their next permanent manager with Iraola the preferred choice to restore stability and build on the foundation left behind.

cards.headline: Spurs force Game 7 against Thunder in Western Conference finals
cards.teaser: San Antonio routed Oklahoma City to set up a decisive seventh game, with the winner advancing to face the Knicks in the NBA Finals.
cards.body:
The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder in a blowout to force a seventh game in the Western Conference finals. The winner will advance to the NBA Finals to face the Knicks.

Former NBA player Paul Pierce suggested the Spurs may have gotten inside the Thunder's heads after another lopsided victory. The decisive Game 7 will determine which team moves on to compete for the championship.

cards.headline: Novak Djokovic loses at French Open to teenager Fonseca
cards.teaser: Djokovic's bid for a 25th Grand Slam title ended with a loss to Brazilian teenager Joao Fonseca, ensuring a new men's major winner.
cards.body:
Novak Djokovic's bid for a 25th Grand Slam title ended in a five-set loss to Brazilian teenager João Fonseca at the French Open. Djokovic won the first two sets 6-4, 6-4 on Court Philippe-Chatrier but could not maintain his lead. Fonseca stormed back to win 4-6, 4-6, 6-3, 7-5, 7-5 in a grueling four-hour match.

The loss guarantees a new men's Grand Slam champion at this year's tournament. The 19-year-old's victory marked a remarkable comeback and showcased his credentials as a rising force in tennis.

cards.headline: Wigan retains Women's Challenge Cup with win over St Helens
cards.teaser: Eva Hunter scored four tries as Wigan thrashed St Helens 54-6 at Wembley to retain the Women's Challenge Cup.
cards.body:
Wigan Warriors retained the Women's Challenge Cup with a dominant 54-6 victory over St Helens at Wembley. Eva Hunter was the standout performer, scoring four tries in a clinical display that showcased the Warriors' superiority throughout the match.

The comprehensive win demonstrated Wigan's control and quality against their rivals, securing back-to-back titles at the iconic London stadium.

cards.headline: Arsenal and PSG fans clash before Champions League final in Budapest
cards.teaser: Police in Budapest made arrests and are reviewing CCTV footage after supporters fought before the Champions League final.
cards.body:
Budapest police have arrested supporters involved in a fight between Arsenal and Paris St-Germain fans ahead of Saturday's Champions League final. Authorities are reviewing CCTV footage to identify additional participants in the violence that erupted as fans gathered in the Hungarian capital.

The incident comes as both sets of supporters prepare for the match in Budapest, with rival fans expressing their passion through their anthems and songs.

cards.headline: Steelers fire assistant coach Derius Swinton after three months
cards.teaser: The Pittsburgh Steelers dismissed special teams assistant Derius Swinton II for violating club policy just months after he joined the team.
cards.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers fired assistant coach Derius Swinton II for violating team policy. Swinton, a senior special teams assistant, had been with the AFC franchise for only three months.

The team did not disclose the nature of the policy violation. Swinton's brief tenure ended abruptly with his dismissal from the coaching staff.

cards.headline: Arsenal and PSG prepare for Champions League final
cards.teaser: Fans of Arsenal and Paris St-Germain filled Budapest with rival songs and anthems ahead of the Champions League final.
cards.body:
Arsenal and Paris St-Germain fans gathered in Budapest ahead of Saturday's Champions League final, singing their club anthems in the buildup to the match. Police investigated a fan brawl before the fixture, making arrests and reviewing CCTV footage to identify those involved.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta confirmed that Dutch defender Jurrien Timber is fit to start after recovering from a groin injury that sidelined him for over two months. Arsenal players including Declan Rice and Leandro Trossard reflected on what winning Europe's top prize would mean to the club.

hero.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remaining 2026 Concerts for Health Reasons
hero.body:
Frankie Valli, the 92-year-old lead singer of The Four Seasons, has canceled all remaining concerts scheduled for 2026 to focus on his health.

The artist announced he will take six months off from performing. Valli cited the need to concentrate on getting well as the reason for the cancellations.

Valli rose to fame in the 1960s as frontman of The Four Seasons, the group behind hits including "Sherry," "Big Girls Don't Cry," and "Walk Like a Man." The band sold more than 100 million records worldwide and was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1990.

The singer has maintained an active touring schedule in recent years despite his age. His performances have drawn audiences who remember the original hits as well as younger fans familiar with the Broadway musical "Jersey Boys," which dramatized the band's story.

Valli has not disclosed specific details about his health condition. The announcement focused on his decision to take time away from the stage rather than on any particular diagnosis or treatment.

The canceled shows were part of a touring schedule that had extended into the latter half of 2026. Ticket holders will receive refunds through their original points of purchase.

Valli indicated he may consider returning to touring in 2027, though he did not commit to specific dates or venues. The decision to resume performing will depend on his recovery during the six-month break.

The singer's career has spanned more than six decades. He has performed both as a solo artist and with various incarnations of The Four Seasons, maintaining recognition across multiple generations of music fans.

Valli's announcement comes as several veteran performers from his era have either reduced their touring schedules or retired from live performance entirely due to age and health considerations.

cards.headline: Arsenal to Face PSG in Champions League Final
cards.teaser: Arsenal F.C. and Paris Saint-Germain F.C. will compete for the UEFA Champions League title in Budapest.
cards.body:
Arsenal will take on Paris Saint-Germain in the 2026 UEFA Champions League Final on Saturday, May 30, at Puskás Aréna in Budapest, Hungary. The Killers will perform during the kick-off show before the match begins.

Mikel Arteta confirmed that Dutch defender Jurrien Timber is fit to start after recovering from a groin injury that sidelined him for over two months. Arsenal players including Leandro Trossard, Declan Rice, and Eberechi Eze have spoken about what winning Europe's most prestigious club trophy would mean to them.

cards.headline: Dmitry Bivol Defends Multiple Light Heavyweight Titles Against Michael Eifert
cards.teaser: Russian boxer Dmitry Bivol puts his IBF, WBA and WBO light heavyweight championship belts on the line in a 12-round bout.
cards.body:
Dmitry Bivol will defend his IBF, WBA and WBO light heavyweight titles against German boxer Michael Eifert in a scheduled 12-round championship match. Bivol currently holds all three belts in the division.

The bout represents a significant test for the Russian champion, who faces a challenger looking to claim multiple world titles in a single fight. One fighter will leave the ring with the championship belts or the contest will conclude in a draw.

cards.headline: Paul McCartney Releases New Album Featuring Song About Eleanor Rigby Story
cards.teaser: The former Beatle's new album includes a track that revisits themes from the classic Beatles song.
cards.body:
At 83, Paul McCartney has released his 20th solo album, "The Boys of Dungeon Lane," which looks back across his six-decade career. The album draws inspiration from formative moments, family memories, and even his own birth, reflecting on themes that have defined his songwriting throughout the years.

The new album continues McCartney's tradition of narrative songwriting established with the Beatles' 1966 classic "Eleanor Rigby." That groundbreaking track told the story of lonely people through spare, literary lyrics backed by string arrangements. McCartney has revisited similar storytelling approaches across his solo work, with songs like "Momma Gets By" representing a full-circle return to these thematic explorations.

cards.headline: Vanilla Ice Plans to Perform at Trump-Backed Festival Despite Artist Dropouts
cards.teaser: The rapper defended his decision to perform at the Freedom 250 festival in Washington, D.C., saying music is not political.
cards.body:
Vanilla Ice said he will keep his scheduled performance at the Freedom 250 festival in Washington, D.C., despite multiple artists canceling their appearances. The event is backed by Donald Trump and scheduled for this summer.

The rapper stated that music is not political and said he would perform for Russian President Vladimir Putin or in Iran if asked.

cards.headline: Pete Davidson Praises Ex-Girlfriend Kim Kardashian on Podcast
cards.teaser: The comedian spoke positively about Kardashian during an appearance on a podcast with Nikki Glaser, almost four years after their split.
cards.body:
Pete Davidson praised his ex-girlfriend Kim Kardashian during a podcast appearance with Nikki Glaser. Davidson called Kardashian "superhuman" and complimented her acting skills, saying "she's so good."

The comments came almost four years after the couple split. Davidson and Kardashian dated for several months before ending their relationship. The comedian rarely speaks publicly about his past relationships.

cards.headline: Larry Lamb Describes Working on EastEnders and Gavin and Stacey Simultaneously
cards.teaser: The British actor recalled juggling roles on two major television series at the same time.
cards.body:
Actor Larry Lamb described himself as lucky to have landed roles on both EastEnders and Gavin and Stacey. He spoke about the experience of working on the sets of both series simultaneously.

Lamb appeared on the BBC soap opera EastEnders and the sitcom Gavin and Stacey, both of which became fixtures of British television. Balancing the two productions required coordination between the different filming schedules and sets.

hero.headline: Defense Secretary disputes claim Iran war delayed Taiwan arms sale
hero.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth rejected assertions from a military official that ongoing conflict with Iran has delayed a $14 billion arms sale to Taiwan. Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao told senators the United States was postponing the deal to protect shrinking munitions supplies.

Hegseth's public disagreement with his acting Navy secretary's testimony highlights internal tensions within the Pentagon over military readiness and weapons inventory management. The split between the two senior defense officials has drawn attention to how the Iran conflict is affecting America's ability to support its allies.

Taiwan has been awaiting the arms package as part of long-standing American commitments to help defend the island against potential military threats. The sale represents one of the largest pending weapons transfers to the region.

Cao's testimony to senators suggested that sustained combat operations in Iran have strained U.S. weapons stockpiles significantly. He indicated the Pentagon needed to carefully manage munitions inventories and restrict major foreign arms sales to address supply concerns.

Hegseth's pushback against this characterization raises questions about whether Pentagon leadership agrees on the severity of weapons supply challenges. The public nature of their disagreement is unusual for the department's top officials.

The timing of the Taiwan sale has become more significant as the United States maintains military operations against Iran. American forces engaged in the conflict consume precision munitions and other weapons systems at substantial rates. Earlier this month, President Trump said he expected additional U.S. military deaths before the Iran conflict concludes, describing casualties as inevitable in war.

The conflict has extended beyond military concerns into economic territory. Energy bills are rising for millions of households, with typical users facing an additional 221 pounds annually under new price caps. U.S. inflation increased at its fastest pace in three years in April, driven largely by higher energy prices tied to the war. Disposable household income has dropped for three consecutive months after adjusting for inflation.

The economic impact is affecting public opinion on Trump's leadership. A Reuters/Ipsos survey showed the president's approval rating fell to near its lowest level since returning to office, with declining support even among Republicans. Trump won the 2024 election largely on promises to reduce inflation.

Neither Hegseth nor Cao has provided specific details about current stockpile levels or the particular weapons systems included in the Taiwan package. The disagreement became public when Hegseth responded to Cao's Senate testimony.

The dispute underscores broader challenges facing the Pentagon as it balances immediate military needs in the Middle East with longer-term commitments to support allies in Asia. Taiwan's defense capabilities remain central to broader U.S. strategic interests in the region.

cards.headline: Former CDC director warns Ebola outbreak could become second largest in history
cards.teaser: Robert Redfield said the current outbreak is already the third-largest spread of the virus globally.
cards.body:
Robert Redfield, former director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, warned that the current Ebola outbreak could become the second-largest in history. He made the comments to NewsNation on Friday.

The outbreak is already the third-largest ever recorded, according to Redfield's assessment. The World Health Organization has also mobilized in response, with its chief traveling to Congo's capital, Kinshasa, to assess containment efforts against the rare strain of Ebola virus spreading in the region.

cards.headline: Attorney General Bondi testified in Epstein investigation
cards.teaser: Former Attorney General Pam Bondi gave testimony in the ongoing Epstein case this week.
cards.body:
Former Attorney General Pam Bondi testified before the House Oversight and Reform Committee on Friday regarding the Department of Justice's handling of Jeffrey Epstein files under her leadership. She defended the department's process while acknowledging "redaction errors" in the files.

Bondi told lawmakers she delegated oversight of the effort to Todd Blanche, her former deputy attorney general who is now serving as acting attorney general. Democratic committee members noted that Bondi declined to answer questions about President Donald Trump's involvement in the release of the files.

cards.headline: Trump defends renovations to Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool
cards.teaser: The president criticized media coverage of the project and described the pool's previous condition as a dump.
cards.body:
President Trump defended his administration's renovations of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, targeting media coverage that has been critical of the project. He described the pool's prior state in harsh terms.

Trump said professionals are now doing the right job for a fraction of previous spending. He singled out The New York Times for continuing to criticize the project, calling the newspaper failing.

cards.headline: Credit card delinquencies reach highest level since 2011
cards.teaser: More than 13 percent of credit card balances were at least 90 days past due in the first quarter.
cards.body:
The share of credit card balances at least 90 days past due climbed above 13 percent in the first quarter. That represents the highest delinquency rate since 2011.

The increase in seriously delinquent accounts signals growing financial stress among cardholders. The last time late payment rates reached this level was during the aftermath of the financial crisis.

cards.headline: Texas Senate race tests durability of Republican cultural messaging
cards.teaser: The contest has become a test case for whether anti-woke politics still resonates amid economic pressures.
cards.body:
The Texas Senate race has become a flashpoint for Republican cultural messaging, with GOP nominee Ken Paxton attacking Democratic state Rep. James Talarico over masculinity after winning the Republican primary runoff. Paxton called Talarico "too low-T for Texas," putting questions about manhood at the center of the campaign.

The race illustrates how Republicans are deploying cultural arguments as a central strategy in 2026, testing whether the messaging that resonated in 2020 remains effective in a different political environment.

cards.headline: Nvidia to debut first Windows PCs with its processors next week
cards.teaser: The chipmaker known for powering AI systems is entering the PC market with Microsoft.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

Nvidia will unveil the first Windows computers using its chips as the main processor next week, sources confirmed. The company best known for AI technology is expanding into the PC market.

Nvidia and Microsoft will present their collaboration at the Computex trade show in Taiwan and Microsoft's Build conference. The debut gives Microsoft a second attempt at AI PCs after its first push encountered difficulties, this time partnered with a leading chipmaker.

---

Reason: The additional source material provided (about NASA's Moon base plans and Myanmar's political tour) relates to entirely different stories and is not relevant to the Nvidia Windows PC announcement.
